name: Nordic hamstring curl
instructions: Kneel on a pad with your ankles anchored under a bench, bar or partner.
Keep your hips extended so your body is straight from knees to head.
Lower forward as slowly as you can (aim for 3–5 s), resisting with the hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands, push lightly back up and repeat. The best-evidenced hamstring injury prevention exercise there is.

name: Copenhagen adductor plank
instructions: Lie on your side with the top leg on a bench: inner knee on the bench is easier, ankle is harder.
Prop up on your forearm and lift your hips until your body is a straight line.
Hold with steady breathing, then switch sides.
Builds the inner-thigh strength that resists late-race adductor cramps and groin strains.

name: Tibialis raise
instructions: Lean your back against a wall with your feet 30–50 cm in front of you.
Keep heels down and legs straight; pull your toes up toward your shins as high as you can.
Lower slowly. Add a plate on your toes to progress.

name: Single-leg eccentric calf raise
instructions: Stand on one foot with the ball of the foot on a step; hold a rail for balance.
Rise up quickly onto the ball of the foot.
Lower for 3 s until the heel is below the step.
Do half the sets with a bent knee to hit the soleus. Both matter for calf cramp resistance.

name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in the hand opposite your standing leg.
Hinge at the hip, reaching the free leg straight back until your torso is near parallel.
Keep hips square and the standing knee soft.
Drive back up through the heel. Control beats load.

name: Cossack squat
instructions: Take a very wide stance, toes slightly out.
Shift to one side and squat deep on that leg while the other stays straight, toes up.
Keep the chest up and the working heel down.
Push back through the middle to the other side.

name: Standing broad jump
instructions: Stand behind a line, feet hip-width apart.
Swing your arms back, dip and jump forward as far as possible.
Land softly on both feet and stick it for 2 s.
Measure from the line to the back of the rearmost heel.

name: Countermovement jump
instructions: Hands on hips, stand tall.
Dip quickly to about a quarter squat and jump straight up as high as you can.
Land softly in the same spot.
Measure with a jump app (e.g. My Jump) or a jump mat. Best of 3.

name: Dead hang
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar, overhand grip, shoulder width.
Arms straight, shoulders gently engaged rather than shrugged up to the ears.
Hold as long as you can. Grip endurance protects every unhooked handle pass.

name: Bent-arm hang
instructions: From the top of a pull-up, lower until your elbows are at about 90° and hold.
Chest up, shoulders down.
This is the unhooked pop-and-hold position. Breathe steadily through the hold.

name: L-sit
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars, dip handles or the floor with straight arms.
Lift your legs straight out in front, parallel to the floor.
Push your shoulders down and hold. Tuck your knees to make it easier.

name: Hollow body hold
instructions: Lie on your back and press your lower back into the floor.
Lift shoulders and legs, arms overhead, body in a shallow banana shape.
Hold without letting the lower back lift.

name: Side plank
instructions: Lie on your side with the elbow under the shoulder.
Lift your hips so your body is straight from head to feet.
Hold. Lift the top leg to make it harder.

name: Bird dog
instructions: On hands and knees, brace your core.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level.
Pause 2 s without the hips rotating, return and switch.

name: Band shoulder pass-through
instructions: Hold a band or stick with a wide grip in front of your hips.
With straight arms, take it overhead and behind you, then back.
Narrow the grip over the weeks as your shoulders open up.

name: Open-book thoracic rotation
instructions: Lie on your side, knees bent to 90°, arms straight out in front.
Open the top arm across your body toward the floor behind you, following it with your eyes.
Keep the knees together. Pause 2 s and return.

name: 90/90 hip switches
instructions: Sit with both knees bent at 90°, one leg in front of you and one to the side.
Rotate both knees to the other side, without your hands if you can.
Pause and lean over the front shin each time.

name: Pigeon stretch
instructions: From all fours, bring one knee forward behind the wrist with the shin angled across.
Extend the back leg straight behind you.
Sink the hips and fold forward over the front leg. Breathe slowly.

name: Couch stretch
instructions: Kneel with one knee against a wall or couch, shin running up it.
Step the other foot forward into a lunge.
Squeeze the back leg's glute and bring your torso upright. The hip-flexor stretch every cyclist needs.

name: Rotational med-ball throw
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall holding a 3–5 kg med ball at your hip.
Load the back hip, then rotate explosively and throw the ball into the wall.
Catch and reset. The power comes from the hips: this is the pop and rotation of your tricks.

name: Single-leg drop landing
instructions: Stand on one leg on a 30–40 cm box.
Step off and land on the same leg.
Stick it for 2 s: knee over toes, hips back, no inward knee collapse.
The most useful knee-protection drill for hard landings.

name: Neck isometrics, 4-way
instructions: Press your hand against your forehead and resist with your neck. No movement.
Repeat pushing on the back of the head and on each side.
10 s each direction at about 50% effort. Protects against whiplash in crashes.

name: Trick visualisation
instructions: Eyes closed, pick one trick.
Run it in real time, first person: approach speed, edge, pop, pass, spotting the landing, riding away.
Include the feel and the sound. Five clean reps per trick. Mental rehearsal measurably speeds up skill learning.
